what_it_does: Buys several gifts for the same named client on different days, each just under the $50 per-receipt cap.
why_it_passes: Every receipt is under the per-receipt cap, so none is flagged on its own.
what_gives_it_away: The same client's name keeps appearing, and the gifts together far exceed the cap.

what_it_does: Files many gifts without naming a recipient, each priced just under $10.
why_it_passes: Under $10 a recipient does not have to be named, so each receipt is acceptable.
what_gives_it_away: A pile of small, anonymous gifts that all sit just below the naming threshold.

what_it_does: Repeatedly buys equipment priced just under $200, the per-item level that needs pre-approval.
why_it_passes: Each item is below the amount that requires approval, so no approval is asked for.
what_gives_it_away: Several similar gadgets, all priced just under the limit, bought close together.

what_it_does: Submits repeated receipts with only a total, each just under $75, the amount above which an itemized list is required.
why_it_passes: Each total is below the itemization threshold, so a bare total is allowed.
what_gives_it_away: The same kind of vendor and the same near-limit totals keep recurring with no detail.

what_it_does: Claims individual meals that repeatedly land at 96-99% of the per-person daily meal cap.
why_it_passes: Each meal is within the daily cap.
what_gives_it_away: Meal after meal lands almost exactly at the cap, which real eating rarely does.

what_it_does: Files team meals repeatedly just under $150, the receipt total above which attendee details are needed.
why_it_passes: Each total is below the amount that triggers attendee documentation.
what_gives_it_away: Repeated team meals at the same place all sit just below the documentation threshold.

what_it_does: Submits the same expense two times under different receipt ids to get paid twice.
why_it_passes: The two submissions have different ids, so neither looks like a repeat by itself.
what_gives_it_away: Two claims show the same merchant, date, amount and items.

what_it_does: Reuses a single pre-approval reference to cover several separate large purchases.
why_it_passes: Each large purchase shows an approval reference, so it looks pre-approved.
what_gives_it_away: The same approval reference is attached to several different purchases.

what_it_does: Repeatedly claims client entertainment on Saturdays and Sundays when there is no trip or client visit, likely personal outings.
why_it_passes: Each dinner is a normal amount for client entertainment.
what_gives_it_away: The claims cluster on weekends with no trip or client visit behind them.

what_it_does: Claims two different hotels for the same night or nights within one trip.
why_it_passes: Each hotel bill looks like a normal night's stay.
what_gives_it_away: Two hotels are billed for the same night, so one is a double claim or a personal stay.

what_it_does: Buys the identical office item every week but from a different stationery shop each time.
why_it_passes: No single merchant repeats, so checks for repeat purchases at one merchant never trigger.
what_gives_it_away: The same item at the same price shows up weekly, which looks like stockpiling or resale.

what_it_does: Attaches meals and transport dated across almost the whole month to one trip that lasts only 1-2 nights.
why_it_passes: Each meal or ride looks like ordinary trip spending.
what_gives_it_away: The dates run far beyond the trip's length, so everyday local spending is being tied to a trip.

what_it_does: Files solo lunches as two-person team meals at one restaurant to gain extra room under the per-person cap, never naming the attendees.
why_it_passes: The total divided by two stays under the per-person cap.
what_gives_it_away: The same restaurant repeats with 'lunch for two' and no names are ever given.

what_it_does: Files household and personal items under the office supplies category.
why_it_passes: The category says office supplies and the amounts are small.
what_gives_it_away: The item descriptions, such as a yoga mat or cushion covers, are not office items.

what_it_does: Buys gourmet gift hampers at gift shops and files them as team meals with token attendee counts.
why_it_passes: It is filed as a meal, so gift recipient naming and per-recipient limits are never applied.
what_gives_it_away: The merchants are gift shops and the item is a gift basket, not a meal.

what_it_does: Files evening and weekend ride-shares of a personal nature as travel under a business trip id.
why_it_passes: Each ride has a trip id and a modest fare.
what_gives_it_away: The ride dates do not match the dates of the trip and fall on evenings and weekends.

what_it_does: Bills the same vendor in amounts that rise in an exact arithmetic progression, as if drawing down a made-up invoice series.
why_it_passes: Each invoice is a plausible amount for office supplies.
what_gives_it_away: The amounts rise by the same fixed step each time.

what_it_does: Claims an identical taxi fare to the cent at the same hour, each time from a different cab company, as if copying a template receipt.
why_it_passes: Each fare is ordinary and each company appears only once.
what_gives_it_away: The fare matches to the cent and the time repeats while only the company name changes.

what_it_does: Submits dinners that are always whole-dollar amounts, each at a different restaurant.
why_it_passes: Each amount is reasonable for a dinner.
what_gives_it_away: Real bills rarely come out to whole dollars every time.

what_it_does: Splits one large team meal into several receipts from different stalls of the same food hall on the same day.
why_it_passes: Each receipt is under the team meal cap.
what_gives_it_away: Same day, same food hall and same headcount on every receipt.

what_it_does: Buys gifts for a client's relatives, such as a wife, child or mother, rather than for the client contact.
why_it_passes: Each gift is small and looks like relationship building.
what_gives_it_away: Every gift goes to a different family member for personal occasions, not to a business contact.

what_it_does: Buys the same item at about the cap for many different clients from different shops.
why_it_passes: Each gift is within the per-recipient cap.
what_gives_it_away: The identical item keeps recurring, which looks like bulk personal shopping spread across names.

what_it_does: Records a large attendee count on client entertainment so the cost per head looks low.
why_it_passes: The cost per head is low enough to pass.
what_gives_it_away: The items billed cover only two or three people, so the attendee count looks inflated.

what_it_does: Claims weekend family outings as client entertainment.
why_it_passes: Each total is a normal amount for entertainment.
what_gives_it_away: The meals fall on weekends at kid-friendly places with children's menus and four attendees.

what_it_does: Bills one hotel stay to two different trip ids with overlapping dates.
why_it_passes: Each trip looks plausible by itself.
what_gives_it_away: The same nights are claimed under both trips.

what_it_does: Submits hotel bills from several hotels that add up to more nights than the declared trip length.
why_it_passes: Each hotel bill is a normal single stay.
what_gives_it_away: Added together the nights exceed the trip, hinting at padded or personal stays.

what_it_does: Adds an overnight hotel and evening spending to a trip declared with zero nights.
why_it_passes: Each receipt looks like normal travel spending.
what_gives_it_away: A trip with no nights has an overnight hotel and evening expenses.

what_it_does: Files meals and taxis on the same date under two different trips in different cities.
why_it_passes: Each receipt fits its own trip.
what_gives_it_away: The employee cannot be in two cities on the same day.

what_it_does: Declares 7-9 attendees at recurring team meals while the items show only 2-3 portions.
why_it_passes: The stated headcount keeps the cost per person low.
what_gives_it_away: The portions billed do not match the number of attendees declared.

what_it_does: Claims a trip meal in one city and a team lunch with no trip in another city on the same day.
why_it_passes: Each meal looks reasonable by itself.
what_gives_it_away: The two cities cannot both be right on the same day.

what_it_does: Reuses one short trip id for routine rides spread over many unrelated weekdays of the month.
why_it_passes: Each ride is small and carries a trip id.
what_gives_it_away: The rides fall on ordinary weekdays well beyond the trip, like a daily commute.

what_it_does: Charges lodging, meals and rides on the weekend after a Monday to Thursday trip has ended.
why_it_passes: Each charge looks like a normal travel expense.
what_gives_it_away: The charges fall after the trip ended and bill more nights than the trip recorded.

what_it_does: Claims the same software as an annual license and also as monthly plan charges in the same month.
why_it_passes: Each charge is a normal software cost.
what_gives_it_away: The same product is billed at two billing cycles.

what_it_does: Claims nearly the same client lunch every Friday at one restaurant, which looks like a personal habit.
why_it_passes: Each lunch is a modest amount.
what_gives_it_away: It recurs on the same weekday at the same restaurant for almost the same amount.

what_it_does: Claims a weekly coffee and tea subscription box as office supplies every week.
why_it_passes: Each box is a small supply-type charge.
what_gives_it_away: The identical box at the same price arrives weekly and is for personal consumption.

what_it_does: Claims weekly passes for a personal meditation and sleep app as software.
why_it_passes: Each pass is a small software-sized charge.
what_gives_it_away: A consumer app is billed in weekly slices, which avoids a monthly review.

what_it_does: Attaches approval references to routine meals, taxis and supplies that never need approval.
why_it_passes: Each receipt carries an approval reference, so it looks authorized.
what_gives_it_away: Approval references on everyday spending serve no purpose and lend false authority.

what_it_does: Uses approval numbers that run in reverse order while the purchase dates run forward.
why_it_passes: Each purchase has an approval reference.
what_gives_it_away: Earlier purchases hold newer approvals, suggesting approvals obtained after the fact or borrowed.

what_it_does: Takes out several software subscriptions with the same function, each under its own approval reference.
why_it_passes: Each subscription has its own approval.
what_gives_it_away: Several tools do the same job, more than one person needs.

what_it_does: Buys 2 to 3 units of a single-user peripheral under one approval reference.
why_it_passes: Each purchase has its own approval and stays inside the per-unit approval.
what_gives_it_away: Quantities of one-person equipment far exceed what one person needs.

what_it_does: Claims both an included service charge and a separate tip of a similar percentage on every dinner.
why_it_passes: Each total is a plausible dinner amount.
what_gives_it_away: Every dinner shows both charges, so gratuity is claimed twice.

what_it_does: Adds the exact same booking fee to rides from four different taxi companies.
why_it_passes: Each ride and fee looks ordinary alone.
what_gives_it_away: Independent companies would not charge the identical fee.

what_it_does: Buys the same box of paper weekly at the same shop with the unit price rising about 6% each time.
why_it_passes: Each purchase is a modest, ordinary amount.
what_gives_it_away: The price of the same item climbs steadily, suggesting inflated or fabricated invoices.

what_it_does: Has four different stationers bill exact consecutive multiples (1x, 2x, 3x, 4x) of one base amount.
why_it_passes: Each amount is plausible for an office purchase.
what_gives_it_away: The amounts are neat multiples of one number, as if made up from it.

what_it_does: Hosts the same named client contact at four different venues within a few weeks.
why_it_passes: Each meal is a normal amount for hosting.
what_gives_it_away: One person is hosted far more often than is usual.

what_it_does: Files a nameless two-person client lunch every Friday at the same small cafe.
why_it_passes: The cost per head is trivial.
what_gives_it_away: It looks like a regular lunch with a colleague, with no client named.

what_it_does: Files cake, decorations and party platters for 9-14 people as client entertainment on one day.
why_it_passes: Each receipt is a modest amount.
what_gives_it_away: Together they match an internal birthday or farewell party, with no client named.

what_it_does: Files a client dinner for three and then an individual dinner at the same restaurant minutes later, so the employee's own meal is claimed twice.
why_it_passes: Each is a normal dinner receipt.
what_gives_it_away: Same restaurant, same evening, minutes apart.

what_it_does: Buys stationery in wholesale quantities, hundreds of pens or sleeves.
why_it_passes: Each purchase is modest in dollar terms.
what_gives_it_away: No single office worker could use such quantities.

what_it_does: Buys small accessories over the month that add up to a complete home streaming studio.
why_it_passes: Each accessory is a small equipment purchase.
what_gives_it_away: Together the items form a ring light, microphone, capture card and webcam setup.

what_it_does: Claims lodging, shuttles and meals at ski or beach resort venues on a business trip.
why_it_passes: Each amount looks like normal travel spending.
what_gives_it_away: All the merchants are leisure resorts, which makes a work purpose implausible.

what_it_does: Files supermarket baskets in family-sized quantities as individual meals.
why_it_passes: Each total is small enough to look like one meal.
what_gives_it_away: The items, such as kilos of chicken or dozens of eggs, are not one person's meals.

what_it_does: Makes no office-supply purchases all month, then four sizeable ones in the last three working days.
why_it_passes: Each purchase is a normal office item.
what_gives_it_away: The spending is bunched at month end, like using up a budget.

what_it_does: Files client dinners time-stamped just after the 05:00 cutoff, between 05:01 and 05:11, on several days.
why_it_passes: Each time is outside the 00:00-05:00 overnight check.
what_gives_it_away: Evening dinners with dawn timestamps look back-dated or edited.

what_it_does: Expenses three or four competing tools with the same function as Pro monthly plans, all sampled once in the same stretch.
why_it_passes: Each monthly plan is a small software charge.
what_gives_it_away: Rival tools doing the same job point to sampling, not a business need.

what_it_does: Claims both a solo dinner and a client dinner at different restaurants within 30 minutes of each other on two evenings.
why_it_passes: Each dinner is acceptable alone.
what_gives_it_away: Both dinners cannot be real that close together.

what_it_does: Repeatedly bills one-night weekday hotel stays in the city where all their everyday receipts are.
why_it_passes: Each stay looks like ordinary lodging.
what_gives_it_away: There is no transport to or from anywhere, so these look like nights at a hotel near home.

what_it_does: Bills a rental car for every day of the trip while also claiming taxis and rideshares in the same city on the same days.
why_it_passes: Each charge is normal ground transport.
what_gives_it_away: The car is clearly in use, so ground transport is paid twice.

what_it_does: Pays airline and rail seat, bag, boarding, lounge and fare charges for two passengers on a solo trip.
why_it_passes: Each charge looks like a normal travel extra.
what_gives_it_away: The traveler has a single room and individual meals, but the extras are for two.

what_it_does: Gives one named client a separate just-under-cap gift on several dates, with a different reason each time.
why_it_passes: Each gift is under the $50 cap as its own occasion.
what_gives_it_away: The total to one person is several times the $50 cap.

readable_name: Weekly Date Night As Client Dinner
what_it_does: Repeats the same two-person client dinner at the same restaurant on the same weekday evening.
why_it_passes: Each dinner is a normal client entertainment amount.
what_gives_it_away: It happens week after week, like a standing personal date night.

what_it_does: Claims cafe breakfasts on mornings when the hotel rate already includes breakfast.
why_it_passes: Each breakfast is a small, ordinary meal.
what_gives_it_away: The hotel bill shows breakfast included every morning.

what_it_does: Buys toner and ink for three incompatible printer families at three different stores in one month.
why_it_passes: Each purchase is an ordinary supply.
what_gives_it_away: One desk or office does not run that many printer types, suggesting personal printers or resale.

what_it_does: Buys portable SSDs, external drives and flash drives in multi-unit quantities across several stores in one month.
why_it_passes: Each unit is a cheap reimbursable accessory.
what_gives_it_away: The quantities are far beyond any single person's need.

what_it_does: Files night-out meals and rides stamped a few minutes after 05:00, just outside the overnight review window.
why_it_passes: Each time falls outside the window.
what_gives_it_away: Dinner and supper items are stamped at dawn, when no restaurant serves them.

what_it_does: Claims computer accessories bought at pet, toy, garden, sporting-goods or craft stores.
why_it_passes: Each is labelled computer equipment at a modest price.
what_gives_it_away: The stores' names and merchant types say they sell something else.

what_it_does: Attaches an approval reference whose number is exactly the purchase date to several large peripheral purchases.
why_it_passes: Each purchase shows a different approval reference.
what_gives_it_away: The references copy the purchase date, so they were made up at purchase time.

what_it_does: Pays an identical flex-space access pass on the same weekday every week and expenses each as a one-off.
why_it_passes: Each pass is a small amount.
what_gives_it_away: Together the passes amount to a standing monthly membership.

what_it_does: Bills dry-cleaning of comforters, drapes and children's uniforms to a trip under the laundry allowance.
why_it_passes: Each ticket is a modest laundry amount on a trip.
what_gives_it_away: A traveler would not carry such items.

what_it_does: Buys every transit ticket and pass for two adults on solo business trips.
why_it_passes: Each fare is small.
what_gives_it_away: The company is paying a companion's fares.

what_it_does: Claims a two-night trip that has no hotel, no transport and only weekday lunches.
why_it_passes: Each lunch is a small, ordinary amount.
what_gives_it_away: The trip has no travel costs, and the lunches are at the usual spots used for team lunches.

what_it_does: Makes three odd-cent supply purchases in the last days of May that bring the month's total to exactly $1,000.00.
why_it_passes: Each purchase is a normal supply amount.
what_gives_it_away: The month's total lands on exactly $1,000.00, like topping up to an allowance.
